questions.q: A body weight $W$, is projected vertically upwards from earth's surface to reach a height above the earth which is equal to nine times the radius of earth. The weight of the body at that height will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Final distance from the centre of earth wil be& $R + 9R = 10R$.

Now acceleration due to gravity at any height(distance from centre r) is given by,

$g = \dfrac{GM}{r2}$.

Therefore,

$g^{'} = \dfrac{GM}{\left(10R\right)2}$

Now, value of~$g$~at surface will be,~$\dfrac{GM}{R2}$.

Hence,

$g^{'} = \left(\dfrac{g}{100}\right).

Then,~$W^{'} = mg^{'} = \dfrac{mg}{100} = \dfrac{W}{100}$

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion $A$~and the other is labelled as Reason $R$.

Assertion $A$~: The escape velocities of planet $A$~and $B$~are same. But $A$~and $B$~are of unequal mass.

Reason $R$:~The product of their mass and radius must be same. ${M}_{1}{R}_{1} = {M}_{2}{R}_{2}$ In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both& $A$ and~$R$ are correct and $R$~is the correct explanation of~$A$
Both& $A$ and $R$~are correct but~$R$ is NOT~the correct explanation of~$A$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${V}_{e} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$

$\dfrac{M1}{R1} = \dfrac{M2}{R2}$

${M}_{1}{R}_{2} = {M}_{2}{R}_{1}$

Hence reason $R$& is not correct.

questions.q: The time period of a satellite, revolving above earth's surface at a height equal to $R$~will be (Given $g = {π}^{2}ms^{- 2}, R =$ radius of earth)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The velocity of the satellite revolving round the Earth at a height& $r$~from the centre of the Earth is given by

$v = \sqrt{ \left(\dfrac{GM}{r}\right)} . . . \left($1\right)$

The formula to calculate the time period in the circular orbit is given by

$T = \dfrac{2\pir}{v} . . . \left($2\right)$

In this case:~$r = R + R = 2R$

Substitute the expression for the velocity from equation (1) into equation (2) and simplify to obtain the required time period.

$\begin{cases}T \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{2\pir}{\dfrac{GM}{r}}\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{2\pi \times 2R}{\dfrac{gR}{2}}\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{4\piR\sqrt{2}}{\pi\sqrt{R}}\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 4\sqrt{2R}\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \sqrt{32R}\end{cases}$

questions.q: Consider a binary star system of star $A$ and star $B$ with masses ${m}_{A}$ and ${m}_{B}$ revolving in a circular orbit of radii ${r}_{A}$ and ${r}_{B},$~respectively. If ${T}_{A}$ and ${T}_{B}$ are the time period of star $A$ and star $B,$ respectively, then:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
1) From the centre of mass, we get

${M}_{1}{R}_{1} = {M}_{2}{R}_{2} - - - - - - 1$

2) Force acting~on both starts i.e. gravitational force and centripetal force are balanced.

$\dfrac{{GM}_{1}{M}_{2}}{R2} = \dfrac{{M}_{1}{V}_{1}^{2}}{R1} = \dfrac{{M}_{1}{V}_{1}^{2}}{R1} - - - - - - 2$

As we know,~${V}_{1} = \dfrac{2{πR}_{1}}{T1} \text{ and } {V}_{2} = \dfrac{2{πR}_{2}}{T2}$

Substituting equation 3 in equation 2, we get~

$\dfrac{{M}_{1}{R}_{1}}{\left({T}_{1}\right)2} = \dfrac{{M}_{1}{R}_{2}}{\left({T}_{2}\right)2} - - - - - - 4$

From equation 1, we conclude in eqution 4

\left({T}_{1}\right)2 = \left({T}_{2}\right)2or{T}_{1} = {T}_{2}$

$

questions.q:
The approximate height from the surface of earth at which the weight of the body becomes $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of its weight on the surface of earth is :
[Radius of earth $R = 6400km$ and $\sqrt{3} = 1 . 732$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The variation of the acceleration due to gravity with height& $h$~is given by,

$g^{'} = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)2}$.

Since the weight at given height is~$\dfrac{1}{3}$~of the weight at the surface

$⇒ g^{'} = \dfrac{g}{3} ⇒ \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)2} = \dfrac{g}{3} ⇒ \left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right) = \sqrt{3} ⇒ h = R\left(\sqrt{3} - 1\right) = 6400 \times \left(1 . 732 - 1\right) = 4685km$

questions.q:
Assume that the earth is a solid sphere of uniform density and a tunnel is dug along its diameter throughout the earth. It is found that when a particle is released in this tunnel, it executes a simple harmonic motion. The mass of the particle is $100g$. The time period of the motion of the particle will be (approximately)

(take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$, radius of earth $= 6400km$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The gravitational force acting on a particle of mass $m$ at a distance$r ( < R )$~from the centre of Earth is

$F = - G\dfrac{M^{'}m}{r2}$~ ....(1)

where~$M^{'}$~is the mass of portion of Earth enclosed by a sphere of radius $r$ concentric with Earth. Here~$-$ sign indicates radially inward~direction of force.

Taking the density of Earth to be uniform

$\dfrac{M '}{4{πr}^{3}} = \dfrac{M}{4{πR}^{3}}$

$⇒ M^{'} = \dfrac{Mr^{3}}{R3}$~ ~....(2)

Substituting~$M^{'}$~from equation 2 into equation 1:

$F = - \left(\dfrac{GMm}{R3}\right)r$

Which is similar to the equation of motion~$F = - kx$~with~$k = G\dfrac{Mm}{R3} = \dfrac{mg}{R} ( ∵ g = G\dfrac{M}{R2} )$

For such motion, the time period is given by:

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$

Substituting k from above,

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R}{g}}$

Putting the values, we get

$T = 2 \times 3 . 14\sqrt{\dfrac{6400 \times {10}^{3}}{10}} = 2 \times 3 . 14 \times 800 \approx 1hour24minutes$

questions.q: The mass of the moon is $\dfrac{1}{144}$ times the mass of a planet and its diameter $\dfrac{1}{16}$ times the diameter of a planet. If the escape velocity on the planet is v, the escape velocity on the moon will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, escape velocity is given by, ${v}_{escape} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$

Now, ${v}_{planet} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}} = v$

${v}_{Moon} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM \times 16}{144 \times R}} = \dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}} = \dfrac{v}{3}$

questions.q: An object is taken to a height above the surface of earth at a distance $\dfrac{5}{4}R$ from the centre of the earth. Where radius of earth, $R = 6400km$. The percentage decrease in the weight of the object will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at& height& $h$ is given by,~$g^{'} = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)2}$

For distance from the centre $r = \dfrac{5}{4}R$~height~$h = \dfrac{R}{4}$,

$⇒ g^{'} = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{4}\right)2} = \dfrac{16}{25}g$

Change in weight~

$∆ W = mg - mg^{'} ⇒ ∆ W = mg \left($1 - $\dfrac{16}{25}\right)

$⇒ ∆ W = $\dfrac{9}{25}$mg$

Percentage change~=\dfrac{9}{25} \times$100 %$

$= 36 %$

$

questions.q: A mass of $50$ kg is placed at the center of a uniform spherical shell of mass $100$ kg and radius $50m$. If the gravitational potential at a point, $25m$ from the center is $Vkgm^{- 1}$. The value of $V$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Use the formula& of the gravitational potential in terms of universal gravitational constant,& $V = \dfrac{- GM}{R}⇒ {V}_{p} = - \dfrac{G ( 100 )}{50} - \dfrac{G ( 50 )}{25}= - 4G$.

questions.q: If $R$ is the radius of the earth and the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is $g = {π}^{2}ms^{- 2}$, then the length of the second's pendulum at a height $h = 2R$ from the surface of earth will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at the given height, $g ' = \dfrac{GM}{\left(3R\right)2} = \dfrac{1}{9}\dfrac{GM}{\left(R\right)2} = \dfrac{1}{9}g$, where $g$ is acceleration due to gravity at the surface of the Earth.

Now, time period is given by, $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g '}}$

Also the time period of second pendulum is $2$ sec.

Therefore, $T = 2sec$

Then, $2 = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g} \times 9}$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{1}{9}m$

questions.q: A planet having mass $9{M}_{e}$~and radius $4{R}_{e},$ where ${M}_{e}$~and ${R}_{e}$~are mass and radius of earth respectively, has escape velocity in $kms^{- 1}$ given by:~(Given escape velocity on earth ${V}_{e} = 11 . 2 \times {10}^{3}ms^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The escape velocity on earth is given by ${V}_{e } = \sqrt{\dfrac{2G{M}_{e}}{Re}}$

Escape velocity for the planet is

$V{'}_{esc} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2G ( 9{M}_{e} )}{4{R}_{e}}} . . . ( i )$

The escape velocity of earth is~${V}_{e} = 11 . 2 \times {10}^{3}ms^{- 1}$

From equation (i)

$V{'}_{esc} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{4}\left(\dfrac{2G{M}_{e}}{Re}\right)} = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 11 . 2 \times {10}^{3}ms^{- 1} ⇒ V{'}_{esc} = 16 . 8kms^{- 1}$

questions.q:
If ${R}_{E}$ be the radius of Earth, then the ratio between the acceleration due to gravity at a depth $r$~below and a height $r$~above the earth surface is:
(Given : $r < {R}_{E}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{gh}{gd} = \dfrac{GM\left({R}_{E} + r\right)2}{GM{R}_E^{3} \left({R}_{E} -r\right)} = {R}_E^{3} \left({R}_{E} +$r\right)2\left({R}_{E} -r\right)$
\dfrac{gd}{gh} = \left({R}_{E} +$r\right)2\left({R}_{E} -r\right){R}_E^{3} = {R}_E^{3} - {R}_{E}r^{2} + r{R}_E^{2} - r^{3}{R}_E^{3} = 1 - r^{2}{R}_E^{2} + $\dfrac{r}{RE} - \left(\dfrac{r}{RE}\right)$3

questions.q: An astronaut takes a ball of mass $m$ from earth to space. He throws the ball into a circular orbit about earth at an altitude of $318.5 \mathrm{~km}$. From earth's surface to the orbit, the change in total mechanical energy of the ball is $x \frac{\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{21 \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}$. The value of $x$ is (take  \left.\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}=6370 \mathrm{~km}\right)$ :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{h}=318.5 \approx\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}{20}\right) \\ & \mathrm{T} \cdot \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{i}}=\frac{-\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}} \\ & \mathrm{T} \cdot \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{-\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{2\left(\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}+\mathrm{h}\right)}=\frac{-\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{2\left(\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}+\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}{20}\right)} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{T} \cdot \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{-10 \mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{21 \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}\end{aligned}$
Change in total mechanical energy
$\begin{aligned} & =\mathrm{TE}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{TE}_{\mathrm{i}} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{\operatorname{Re}}\left[1-\frac{10}{21}\right]=\frac{11 \mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{21 \operatorname{Re}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two planets A and B of radii $R$~and $1 . 5R$ have densities $ρ$ and $\dfrac{ρ}{2}$ respectively. The ratio of acceleration due to gravity at the surface of B to A is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The acceleration due to gravity is&

$g = \dfrac{GM}{R2} = \dfrac{4\piGRρ}{3} ⇒ g ∝ ρ \cdot R$

Thus, the ratio is~

$⇒ \dfrac{gB}{gA} = \dfrac{1 . 5Rρ}{2ρR} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 . 5 = 0 . 75 ⇒ \dfrac{gB}{gA} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.q: If earth has a mass nine times and radius twice to the of a planet $P$. Then $\dfrac{ve}{3}\sqrt{x}ms^{- 1}$ will be the minimum velocity required by a rocket to pull out of gravitational force of $P$, where ve is escape velocity on earth. The value of $x$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the escape velocity \left({v}_{e}\right)$~for the Earth is given by

${v}_{e} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2G{M}_{e}}{Re}} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

where,~$G$~is the Universal Gravitational constant,~${M}_{e}$~is the mass and~${R}_{e}$~is the radius of Earth.

The formula for the escape velocity~ \left({v}_{esc}\right)$~of any planet is given by

${v}_{esc} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 2 )$

where,~$M$~is the mass and~$R$~is the radius of the planet.

Given that the mass of the planet is~$9$~times the mass of the Earth and the radius of the planet is~$2$~times the radius of the Earth.

Substitute~$\dfrac{Me}{9}$~for~$M$~and~$\dfrac{Re}{2}$~for~$R$~into equation (2) and simplify to obtain the escape velocity for the planet in terms of that in Earth.

$\begin{cases}{v}_{esc} & = & \sqrt{\dfrac{2G\dfrac{Me}{9}}{\dfrac{Re}{2}}} \\ = & \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{2G{M}_{e}}{Re}} \\ = & \dfrac{2}{3}{v}_{e} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 3 )\end{cases}$

Comparing equation (3) with the given expression, it can be written that

$x = 2$.

questions.q: Consider a planet in some solar system that has a mass double the mass of earth and density equal to the average density of the earth. If the weight of an object on earth is $W$, the weight of the same object on that planet will be:
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: A body of mass is taken from earth surface to the height $h$~equal to twice the radius of earth $( {R}_{e} )$, the increase in potential energy will be : ($g =$ acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The potential energy of a particle at a distance& $r ( > {R}_{e} )$~ from the centre of Earth is,

$U = - G\dfrac{{M}_{e}m}{r}$

Initially, the particle is at a height ${R}_{e}$~from the surface. Therefore,~$r = {R}_{e}$.

$∴ {U}_{i} = - G\dfrac{{M}_{e}m}{Re}$

When height is increased to $2{R}_{e}$~from surface,~$r = 2{R}_{e} + {R}_{e} = 3{R}_{e}$

$∴ {U}_{f} = - G\dfrac{{M}_{e}m}{3{R}_{e}}$

Thus, the change in potential energy is

$∆ U = {U}_{f} - {U}_{i} = - G\dfrac{{M}_{e}m}{3{R}_{e}} + G\dfrac{{M}_{e}m}{Re} = \dfrac{2}{3}G\dfrac{{M}_{e}m}{Re} = \dfrac{2}{3}G\dfrac{Me}{{R}_{e}2}m{R}_{e} = \dfrac{2}{3}mg{R}_{e} \left(\text{as}$g = G\dfrac{Me}{{R}_{e}2}\right)$

$

questions.q: A simple pendulum doing small oscillations at a place $\mathrm{R}$ height above earth surface has time period of $T_1=4 \mathrm{~s}$. $T_2$ would be it's time period if it is brought to a point which is at a height $2 \mathrm{R}$ from earth surface. Choose the correct relation $[R=$ radius of earth $]$ :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}_1=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\ell}{\mathrm{GM}}(2 \mathrm{R})^2} \\ & \mathrm{~T}_2=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\ell}{\mathrm{GM}}(3 \mathrm{R})^2} \\ & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
The ratio of escape velocity of a planet to the escape velocity of earth will be:-

Given: Mass of the planet is $16$ times mass of earth and radius of the planet is $4$ times the radius of earth.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the escape velocity is given by

${v}_{e} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}} . . . \left(1\right)$

For the Earth, it is given by

${ve}^{E} = $\sqrt{\dfrac{2G{M}_{E}}{RE}} . . . \left(2\right)$

~and, for the planet, it is given by

${ve}^{P} = $\sqrt{\dfrac{2G{M}_{P}}{RP}} . . . \left(3\right)$

Divide equation (2) by equation (3) and simplify to obtain the required ratio.

$\dfrac{{v}_{e}E}{{v}_{e}P} = \sqrt{\dfrac{ME}{MP}} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{RP}{RE}} . . . \left(4\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (4) to obtain the required ratio.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{{v}_{e}E}{{v}_{e}P} & = & \sqrt{\dfrac{ME}{16{M}_{E}}} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{4{R}_{E}}{RE}} \\ = & \dfrac{1}{2} \\ ⇒ & {ve}^{P}: {ve}^{E} = 2: 1\end{cases}$

questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity at height $h$ above the earth if~$h ≪ R$ (Radius of earth) is given by
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The acceleration due to gravity& $g '$~at a height~$h$~from the surface of Earth is given by

$g^{'} = \dfrac{GM}{( R + h{)}^{2}} . . . \left(1\right)$

Use the method of binomial expansion to obtain the approximate expression for the acceleration due to gravity at a particular height from the surface of the Earth.

$\begin{cases}g^{'} & = & \dfrac{GM}{R^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)2}\\ & = & \dfrac{GM}{R2}\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)-2 \\ & \approx& \dfrac{GM}{R2}\left(1 - \dfrac{2h}{R}\right) . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$$

The formula to calculate the acceleration due to gravity at the surface of the Earth is given by

$g = $\dfrac{GM}{R2} . . . ($3 )$

Divide equation (2) by equation (3) and simplify to obtain the required relation.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{g '}{g}& = & \dfrac{\dfrac{GM}{R2} \left(1 - \dfrac{2h}{R}\right)}{GMR^{2}}\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \left(1 - \dfrac{2h}{R}\right)\\ \text{ and } ⇒ \text{ and } g ' = g\left(1 - \dfrac{2h}{R}\right)\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: Two satellites $A$ and $B$ move round the earth in the same orbit. The mass of $A$ is twice the mass of $B$. The quantity which is same for the two satellites will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the speed of a satellite while revolving around the Earth is given by

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{G{M}_{e}}{R}} . . . \left(1\right)$

where,~$v$~is the speed,~$G$~is the Gravitational constant,~${M}_{e}$~is the mass of the Earth,~$R& is the radius of the orbit.

As can be seen from the equation, speed is& independent of mass of satellite.

Hence, the speed of the satellites will be the same.

$

questions.q: The weight of a body on the surface of the earth is $100N$. The gravitational force on it when taken at a height, from the surface of earth, equal to one-fourth the radius of the earth is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The& acceleration due to gravity changes as one goes to a height from the surface of the earth. Let the new acceleration due to gravity be& $g '$. The formula for acceleration due to gravity at a height is given by~$g ' = \dfrac{gR^{2}}{\left(R + h\right)2}$

The weight of the body on surface is~$W = mg = 100N$

The weight at the given height is~$W = mg '$.

$⇒ W ' = 100 \times \dfrac{R2}{\left(R + \dfrac{R}{4}\right)2} ⇒ W ' = 100 \times \dfrac{R2}{\dfrac{25R^{2}}{16}} = 64N$

questions.q: The escape velocities of two planets $AandB$ are in the ratio $1: 2$. If the ratio of their radii respectively is $1: 3$, then the ratio of acceleration due to gravity of planet $A$ to the acceleration of gravity of planet $B$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the mass& \left(M\right)$~of any planet of radius~$R$~and density~$ρ$, considering it to be a sphere,~is given by

$M = \dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}ρ . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

The escape velocity~ \left({v}_{A}\right)$~for planet A can be expressed as

$\begin{cases}{V}_{A} & = & \sqrt{\dfrac{2G{M}_{A}}{RA}} \\ & = & \sqrt{\dfrac{2G{ρ}_{A}\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{RA}^{3}}{RA}} \\ & = & C\sqrt{{ρ}_{A} .}{R}_{A} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 2 )\end{cases}$

where,~$G$~is Gravitational constant and~$C = \sqrt{\dfrac{8\piG}{3}}$~is a constant.

Similarly, the escape velocity~ \left({v}_{B}\right)$ of planet B can be expressed as

${v}_{B} = C\sqrt{{ρ}_{B}}{R}_{B} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 3 )$

Divide equation (2) by equation (3) and solve with the known parameters to obtain the ratio of the densities of the planets.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{VA}{VB} & = & \dfrac{C\sqrt{{ρ}_{A}}{R}_{A}}{C\sqrt{{ρ}_{B}}{R}_{B}} \\ \sqrt{\dfrac{ρA}{ρB}} & = & \dfrac{{V}_{A}{R}_{B}}{{V}_{B}{R}_{A}} \\ \dfrac{ρA}{ρB} & = & \left(\dfrac{{V}_{A}{R}_{B}}{{V}_{B}{R}_{A}}\right)2 \\ & = & \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{1}\right)2 \\ & = & \dfrac{9}{4} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 4 )\end{cases}$

The acceleration due to gravity~ \left({g}_{A}\right)$~for planet A is given by

$\begin{cases}{g}_{A} & = & \dfrac{G{M}_{A}}{{R}_{A}2} \\ = & \dfrac{G\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{RA}^{3} \times {ρ}_{A}}{{R}_{A}2} \\ = & \dfrac{C2}{2}{ρ}_{A}{R}_{A} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 5 )\end{cases}$

Similarly, the acceleration due to gravity~ \left({g}_{B}\right)$~can be expressed as

${g}_{B} = \dfrac{C2}{2}{ρ}_{B}{R}_{B} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 6 )$

Divide equation (5) by equation (6) and solve with the help of known parameters to calculate the required ratio of the accelerations due to gravity in both the planets.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{gA}{gB} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{C2}{2}{ρ}_{A}{R}_{A}}{\dfrac{C2}{2}{ρ}_{B}{R}_{B}} \\ = & \dfrac{ρA}{ρB}\dfrac{RA}{RB} \\ = & \dfrac{9}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{3} \\ = & \dfrac{3}{4}\end{cases}$

$= \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{R2}{R1} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$

questions.q: $T$ is the time period of simple pendulum on the earth's surface. Its time period becomes $xT$ when taken to a height $R$ (equal to earth's radius) above the earth's surface. Then, the value of $x$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Time period of a simple pendulum at Earth's surface is given by

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$.

When distance from centre of Earth, i.e.,~at~$h = R$, acceleration due to gravity is~$g ' = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)2} = \dfrac{g}{\left(2\right)2} = \dfrac{g}{4}$

Now, time period is~$xT = 2\pi\sqrt{l\left(\dfrac{g}{4}\right)}$

$⇒ xT = 2 \times 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$

$⇒ xT = 2T ⇒ x = 2$

Thus, $x = 2$.
